item.title: Tesoro EEUU mantendrá calendario de subastas de deuda a pesar del aumento de las recompras: Bessent
item.description: El Tesoro de Estados Unidos seguirá adelante con sus subastas de deuda programadas habitualmente, incluidas las de bonos a largo plazo, a pesar de su decisión de aumentar el volumen de recompra de títulos con vencimientos de entre 10 y 30 años, dijo el lunes el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: El Tesoro de Estados Unidos seguirá adelante con sus subastas de deuda programadas habitualmente, incluidas las de bonos a largo plazo, a pesar de su decisión de aumentar el volumen de recompra de títulos con vencimientos de entre 10 y 30 años, dijo el lunes el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent. Al ser preguntado en una rueda de prensa centrada en las sanciones a Irán sobre los planes del Tesoro respecto a las recompras de bonos y el volumen de las subastas de cara al futuro, Bessent dijo que el departamento "continuará con nuestro programa habitual de subastas" anunciado este mes. Añadió que el Tesoro aún no ha comprado ningún bono en el marco de las recompras ampliadas, que comenzarán el 10 de septiembre para los títulos a 10 y 20 años. Bessent, un ex gestor de fondos de cobertura con experiencia en deuda soberana y mercados de divisas, sorprendió la semana pasada al mercado de bonos de todo el mundo al anunciar que el Tesoro duplicaría el volumen de sus recompras trimestrales de deuda a más largo plazo después de que sus rendimientos alcanzaran los niveles más altos en casi dos décadas. La táctica del responsable del Tesoro contribuyó a reducir los rendimientos de los bonos a 10 años y de los bonos a 20 y 30 años durante un breve periodo de tiempo, lo que proporcionó al Gobierno cierto respiro frente a los elevados retornos que están disparando rápidamente los costos del servicio de la deuda federal. Sin embargo, los rendimientos de los bonos con vencimientos más largos se habían recuperado en gran medida de esas caídas al final de la semana. El lunes registraban un ligero descenso. Bessent también advirtió el lunes a los países que cortaran sus vínculos comerciales con Irán, amenazándolos con sanciones secundarias si no lo hacían, aunque sin llegar a imponer sanciones severas. Advirtió de que esta semana se produciría un importante anuncio de sanciones relacionado con un banco. No ha indicado la fuente de financiación para las recompras del Tesoro, pero la Cuenta General del Tesoro (TGA, por su sigla en inglés) en la Reserva Federal constituye una de las fuentes. Recurrir a esa cuenta evitaría la necesidad de financiar las recompras mediante la emisión de nuevos bonos del Tesoro a más corto plazo, pero mermaría las reservas de efectivo del país. A diferencia de la Fed, el Tesoro no tiene la capacidad de crear dinero a voluntad, por lo que debe financiar las recompras con los recursos de tesorería existentes o solicitar préstamos. Cualquier préstamo adicional debería realizarse a plazos más cortos para no socavar el objetivo de las recompras, que es impulsar la liquidez en el mercado de bonos a más largo plazo. La TGA es, en esencia, la cuenta corriente del Gobierno federal, que se utiliza para sufragar las operaciones diarias del Gobierno, como los salarios de los funcionarios federales, los contratos de defensa y las obligaciones del Tesoro en concepto de intereses y capital. El miércoles pasado ascendía a unos 940.000 millones de dólares. El Tesoro ha reforzado la TGA este año, en parte para pagar unos 166.000 millones de dólares en reembolsos que debe a los importadores, después de que la Corte Suprema del país dictaminara este año que una parte importante de los aranceles a la importación del presidente Donald Trump eran ilegales. Durante el último año, ha registrado un promedio de unos 840.000 millones de dólares, la cifra más alta jamás registrada, salvo durante su rápido aumento durante la pandemia de COVID-19. Un TGA más elevado podría servir de colchón en caso de que los demócratas tomaran el control del Congreso en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura e intentaran utilizar el plazo del techo de deuda como palanca para obtener concesiones de la Casa Blanca.

item.title: Lula's campaign considers curbing on independent contractors in potential new term
item.description: The Brazilian government is evaluating mechanisms to curb the use of workers hired as legal entities rather than employees in a potential reelection of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Brazilian government is evaluating mechanisms to curb the use of workers hired as legal entities rather than employees in a potential reelection of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Monday. The plan could minimize Brazil's pension deficit, and provide higher social security protection for workers, Durigan told Broadcast, the news service of local newspaper Estadao. "A company that has 80% of its workforce employed as independent contractors, you may eventually require that firm to make a social security contribution," he said. Workers hired as legal entities often earn higher gross pay, while firms typically benefit from lower labor costs because they are not required to pay payroll taxes, severance-fund contributions or other benefits. Durigan was introduced by Broadcast as a representative of Lula's presidential campaign, who will seek reelection in the upcoming October vote. Durigan also advocated for a corporate taxation review, citing discussions over payroll taxes and the interest on equity, a type of shareholder remuneration.

item.title: Ibovespa avança em pregão com Braskem e Yduqs sob holofotes
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta segunda-feira, apoiado principalmente pelo forte avanço da Vale, em pregão com noticiário corporativo intenso, incluindo decisão da Braskem de pedir recuperação extrajudicial e anúncio entre Yduqs e Afya sobre conversas para possível combinação de negócios.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta segunda-feira, apoiado principalmente pelo forte avanço da Vale, em pregão com noticiário corporativo intenso, incluindo decisão da Braskem de pedir recuperação extrajudicial e anúncio entre Yduqs e Afya sobre conversas para possível combinação de negócios. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) subiu 0,51%, a 171.906,72 pontos, abandonando a fraqueza dos primeiros negócios, quando recuou a 169.330,39. Na máxima do dia, alcançou 173.109,43 pontos. O volume financeiro somou R$25,33 bilhões. De acordo com analistas do Itaú BBA, o Ibovespa está em recuperação após as quedas recentes e perto de sair da tendência de baixa. "Porém, até que sejam superados os 173.000 pontos (no fechamento), esse movimento deverá ser interpretado como um repique dentro da tendência principal de baixa", afirmaram no relatório Diário do Grafista. Na última sexta-feira, o Ibovespa [USN:L6N44I12B TEXT:"avançou"] 1,85%, a 171.031,73 pontos, cravando três altas seguidas e acumulando alta de 2,45% na semana. No mês, porém, o desempenho permanece com sinal negativo. Mesmo com a alta nesta sessão, ainda cai 3,42%. A pauta da segunda-feira também incluiu [USN:L6N44L0KX TEXT:"pesquisa"] BTG/Nexus mostrando que a vantagem numérica do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) diminuiu para 1 ponto percentual. Ambos seguem em empate técnico. Na visão do chefe de alocação de investimentos e sócio da AW Capital, Gabriel Magno, o levantamento apoiou o tom positivo na bolsa paulista, uma vez que corrobora um cenário de eleição mais acirrada. DESTAQUES VALE ON (VALE3.SA) subiu 2,8%, endossada pelo avanço dos futuros do [USN:L6N44L0K5 TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China, em meio a novos sinais de estímulo de Pequim e pelas expectativas de uma demanda mais forte antes do pico da temporada de construção, em setembro. O contrato mais negociado na Bolsa de Mercadorias de Dalian fechou o pregão do dia com alta de 1,27%. CSN MINERAÇÃO ON (CMIN3.SA) avançou 1,19%. PETROBRAS PN recuou 2,31%, em dia de queda do petróleo no exterior , tendo ainda como pano de fundo o pedido de recuperação extrajudicial da Braskem, na qual a petrolífera divide o controle com a IG4 Capital. ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN fechou com acréscimo de 0,34%, em dia positivo para os bancos do Ibovespa. BRADESCO PN subiu 0,18%, BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) avançou 0,92% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT encerrou em alta de 0,34%. YDUQS ON (YDUQ3.SA) disparou 12,83%, após o grupo de educação informar que mantém [USN:L1N44L0LD TEXT:"tratativas"] "em estágio inicial" com a Afya (AFYA.O) para uma possível combinação de negócios envolvendo as empresas. BRASKEM caiu 6,71% após divulgar que seu conselho de administração aprovou o ajuizamento de pedido de [USN:L1N44L0DH TEXT:"recuperação extrajudicial"] da petroquímica e de certas controladas para reestruturar dívidas de cerca de US$10,9 bilhões. O plano inclui uma possível capitalização via oferta de ações. Em linha com o regulamento da bolsa, a B3 informou que as ações da companhia serão excluídas de seus índices após o encerramento do pregão regular da terça-feira. USIMINAS PNA saltou 8,7%, tendo no radar nota do colunista Lauro Jardim, de O Globo, de que o acionista controlador Ternium (TX.N) quer fechar o capital da companhia. Procurada pela Reuters, a Ternium não comentou de imediato. CSN ON (CSNA3.SA) , que detém ações da Usiminas, avançou 7,72%. Ainda no setor, GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) perdeu 0,05%. SUZANO ON (SUZB3.SA) valorizou-se 3%, respaldada por relatório de analistas do Bank of América, que elevaram a recomendação dos papéis para compra ante neutra, bem como o preço-alvo das ações para R$61. ONCOCLÍNICAS ON (ONCO3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, disparou 32,17%, a R$1,52, em sessão na véspera de um [USN:L6N44L0VP TEXT:"julgamento"] na Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) de recursos contra o entendimento de área técnica da autarquia sobre a não realização de uma oferta pública de aquisição (OPA) das ações da companhia.

item.title: Netanyahu afirma que Irán intentó asesinar a uno de sus hijos
item.description: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el lunes que Irán había intentado asesinar a uno de sus hijos, pero no dio detalles sobre cuándo tuvo lugar el supuesto complot, a qué hijo iba dirigido ni hasta qué punto estuvo cerca de llevarse a cabo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmó el lunes que Irán había intentado asesinar a uno de sus hijos, pero no dio detalles sobre cuándo tuvo lugar el supuesto complot, a qué hijo iba dirigido ni hasta qué punto estuvo cerca de llevarse a cabo. La acusación de Netanyahu pone de relieve el recrudecimiento de las tensiones desde que comenzó en febrero la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, durante la cual murieron el líder supremo, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei, y otros altos dirigentes iraníes. Netanyahu, cuya coalición va a la zaga en las encuestas de opinión a dos meses de las elecciones generales de octubre, hizo esta afirmación en una entrevista telefónica con el Canal 14 de Israel. Respondía así a reportes de que uno de los organismos de seguridad israelíes se había negado a proporcionar protección a un rival político de cara a las elecciones nacionales. "En cuanto a mis hijos (...) Aquí, creo que hay algo bastante increíble, sí. Irán puso en el punto de mira a uno de mis hijos. Irán intentó matar, asesinar a uno de mis hijos", declaró Netanyahu al canal conservador, conocido por su cobertura favorable al Gobierno. "Irán intentó asesinar a uno de mis hijos y, por lo tanto, esta protección de seguridad no es un lujo", afirmó, sin dar más detalles sobre el supuesto complot. No quedó claro de inmediato a cuál de sus hijos se refería. El hijo mayor de Netanyahu, Yair, vive en Miami. La misión de Irán ante Naciones Unidas en Nueva York no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios sobre la acusación. Netanyahu también afirmó que le había dicho al jefe de la agencia de seguridad Shin Bet, David Zini, que se debía proporcionar la seguridad adecuada a cualquier candidato a primer ministro. Los medios de comunicación israelíes habían informado anteriormente que Zini se había negado a proporcionar protección al exjefe militar Gadi Eisenkot y había comunicado a la autoridad electoral del país que no existía ningún complot para atentar contra él. Se prevé que el partido de Eisenkot obtenga el mayor número de escaños en las elecciones, aunque los gobiernos israelíes suelen formarse mediante coaliciones entre varios grupos, en lugar de que un único partido consiga por sí solo la mayoría parlamentaria.

item.title: US Treasury to stick to debt auction schedule despite bigger buybacks, Bessent says
item.description: The U.S. Treasury will continue with its regularly scheduled debt auctions, including for long-dated bonds, despite its move to increase buyback sizes of 10- to 30-year securities, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Treasury will continue with its regularly scheduled debt auctions, including for long-dated bonds, despite its move to increase buyback sizes of 10- to 30-year securities, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday. Asked at a news conference focused on Iran sanctions about Treasury's plans for bond buybacks and auction sizes going forward, Bessent said the department would "continue with our regular program of auctions" [USN:L1N4400V0 TEXT:"announced in early August"]. He added that the Treasury hasn't purchased any bonds yet in the enlarged buybacks, which will start on September 10 for 10- and 20-year securities. Bessent, a former hedge fund manager with extensive experience in sovereign debt and currency markets, last week surprised global bond investors by announcing the Treasury would [USN:L1N44G0GD TEXT:"double the size"] of its quarterly repurchases of longer-dated bonds after their yields reached the highest levels in nearly two decades. The Treasury chief's tactic helped bring down yields on 10-year Treasury notes and 20- and 30-year bonds for a short time, providing the administration some relief from the high bond yields that are rapidly driving up federal debt service costs. But yields on the longer-dated maturities had largely retraced those drops by the end of the week. They were down modestly on Monday. Bessent also warned countries on Monday to [USN:L1N44L0FC TEXT:"cut business ties to Iran"], threatening them with secondary sanctions if they failed to do so, while stopping short of imposing severe penalties. He warned that a major sanctions announcement related to a bank would happen later this week. He has not indicated the funding source for the Treasury buybacks, but the Treasury General Account at the Federal Reserve provides one source. Tapping that account would spare the need to finance the buybacks by issuing new, shorter-dated Treasuries, but would eat into the nation's cash reserves. Unlike the Fed, the Treasury does not have the ability to create money at will, so it needs to pay for the buybacks from existing cash resources or borrow the funds. Any additional borrowing would need to be done at shorter maturities so as not to upend the goal of the buybacks, which is to boost liquidity in the market for longer-dated bonds. The TGA is essentially the federal government's checking account, used to pay for daily government operations like federal worker salaries, defense contracts and Treasury interest and principal obligations. It stood at about $940 billion as of last Wednesday. Treasury has beefed up the TGA this year in part to pay for some $166 billion of refunds it owes to importers after the U.S. Supreme Court earlier this year ruled a major chunk of President Donald Trump's import tariffs [USN:L1N3ZG0JK TEXT:"were illegal"]. Over the last year it has averaged about $840 billion, the highest ever outside of its rapid run-up during the COVID-19 pandemic. A bigger TGA could act as a cushion in the event Democrats take control of Congress in the midterm elections and try to use a debt ceiling deadline as leverage to extract concessions from the White House. INCREASINGLY INTERVENTIONIST APPROACH Bessent has argued the upswing in yields to nearly two-decade highs was unwarranted against the vibrancy of the U.S. economy. He also pointed to the Trump administration's plans to curtail government spending that has driven the collective U.S. IOU to the world north of [USN:L6N44G17Z TEXT:"$40 trillion"]. In the latest of Bessent's increasingly interventionist maneuvers, the Treasury last week said it would double its bond buybacks in the 10- to 30-year sector over the next quarter to at least $4 billion per operation. Bessent, who earlier this month executed the first joint intervention in the Japanese yen in 15 years, said last week that his objective was to support liquidity in an area of the market that is thinly traded, especially in August, while having to compete with a large volume of corporate issuance at higher yields, including for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Rockies place LHP Kyle Freeland (neck) on 15-day IL
item.description: The Colorado Rockies placed veteran left-hander Kyle Freeland on the 15-day injured list with a pinched nerve in his neck and selected the contract of right-hander Blake Adams from Triple-A Albuquerque.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Colorado Rockies placed veteran left-hander Kyle Freeland on the 15-day injured list with a pinched nerve in his neck and selected the contract of right-hander Blake Adams from Triple-A Albuquerque. Freeland, 33, departed his start against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday in the fourth inning with discomfort in his left arm caused by the pinched nerve. He is 4-10 with a 6.37 ERA in 23 starts this season. In 10 major league seasons, all with the Rockies, the Denver native is 69-100 with a 4.71 ERA in 259 appearances (254 starts). Adams, 25, is set to make his major league debut. In 25 appearances (two starts) between Double-A and Triple-A this season, Adams is 3-5 with a 6.52 ERA. The 13th-round draft pick in 2022 has spent five seasons in the minor leagues. --Field Level Media

item.title: Popularidad Trump, en mínimos históricos mientras cae apoyo EEUU a guerra contra Irán: sondeo Reuters/Ipsos
item.description: El apoyo de la opinión pública estadounidense a la guerra con Irán ha caído a su nivel más bajo desde los primeros días del conflicto, lo que ha contribuido a que la popularidad del presidente Donald Trump se mantenga en mínimos históricos, según una encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos que finalizó el lunes.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: El apoyo de la opinión pública estadounidense a la guerra con Irán ha caído a su nivel más bajo desde los primeros días del conflicto, lo que ha contribuido a que la popularidad del presidente Donald Trump se mantenga en mínimos históricos, según una encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos que finalizó el lunes. La encuesta, realizada durante cuatro días, reveló que solo el 31% de los estadounidenses apoya la acción militar de Estados Unidos contra Irán, lo que supone un descenso respecto al 37% registrado en una encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos de marzo y al 34% de principios de este mes. Este descenso se debe a que son menos los que se identifican como republicanos y respaldan el conflicto. Alrededor del 69% de los encuestados republicanos apoya la guerra, frente al 77% de marzo. La guerra ha lastrado la popularidad de Trump este año y, por segunda encuesta consecutiva, solo el 33% de los consultados afirmó que aprobaba la actuación del republicano en la Casa Blanca, el nivel más bajo registrado en los sondeos desde el primer o el segundo mandato de Trump. Alrededor del 83% de la población cree que la guerra se prolongará "durante un largo periodo de tiempo", según la encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos, lo que supone un aumento respecto al 80% previamente en el mes. La encuesta se realizó entre 1.215 adultos estadounidenses de todo el país y tuvo un margen de error de 3 puntos porcentuales.

item.title: German state leader urges joint action to avert Volkswagen plant closures
item.description: Volkswagen's stakeholders must work together on solutions for the auto group in order to shield industry in its home state, the state premier of Lower Saxony said on Monday, as the company tries to avoid plant closures.
item.dc:creator: Rachel More
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen's stakeholders must work together on solutions for the auto group in order to shield industry in its home state, the state premier of Lower Saxony said on Monday, as the company tries to avoid plant closures. "Lower Saxony is automotive country ... and this must remain so," State Premier Olaf Lies said at the VW factory in Hanover, one of five belonging to the group that are facing possible closure. Lies, who sits on the company's supervisory board together with the owner families and labour representatives, spoke ahead of a series of workers' assemblies this week, during which staff will have their first chance to question CEO Oliver Blume on his proposed restructuring. Blume has warned that some 50,000 job cuts are needed to make the carmaker competitive, on top of 50,000 already agreed across the group, which is battling to cut costs to address Chinese competition and billions in U.S. tariff costs. The supervisory board has blocked key elements of his restructuring and is next set to meet on September 4, according to sources familiar with the matter. "Now it is important to me that we find joint solutions," Lies said. Works council chief Daniela Cavallo, who speaks on behalf of Volkswagen's German workforce and also sits on the supervisory board, said the scale of the challenge was clear but reiterated her opposition to plant closures or compulsory redundancies. "A programme for the future can't be created or sustained simply by talking about reducing labour costs, cutting staff, and questioning the viability of locations," Cavallo said in Hanover. "Where is our company actually headed?"

item.title: WikiHow sues OpenAI for copyright infringement over AI training
item.description: Do-it-yourself website WikiHow sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court for allegedly misusing its instructional material to train its popular chatbot ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Do-it-yourself website WikiHow sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court for allegedly misusing its instructional material to train its popular chatbot ChatGPT. WikiHow's lawsuit , filed on Friday, said that the AI company scraped thousands of its how-to articles to help train ChatGPT to respond to human prompts. The lawsuit is part of a wave of cases brought by publishers, authors and other copyright holders against AI companies over the alleged misuse of their material to train chatbots like ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Meta's Llama and Google's Gemini. An OpenAI spokesperson said on Monday that the company's AI models are "trained on publicly available data and grounded in fair use." Spokespeople and attorneys for wikiHow did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the new lawsuit on Monday. WikiHow publishes instructional articles on "subjects ranging from routine tasks to specialized skills," the company said in its complaint. The lawsuit said that OpenAI scraped more than 11,000 of its articles without permission to train its GPT large language models. WikiHow also said that ChatGPT reproduces its text in response to user prompts and threatens to displace its market. "Having ingested wikiHow’s articles, those models now produce competing how-to content on the same subjects, at a fraction of the time, effort, and cost of researching, writing, and editing a wikiHow article," the lawsuit said. "The substitution cuts wikiHow’s revenue and, over time, its reason to keep producing the articles at all." The lawsuit alleges OpenAI copied WikiHow's work "at scale" and infringed at least 1,200 of WikiHow's registered copyrights. WikiHow requested an unspecified amount of monetary damages and a court order blocking OpenAI from infringing its copyrights. The case is WikiHow Inc v. OpenAI Inc, U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, No. 1:26-cv-07171. For WikiHow: Rohit Nath and Alejandra Salinas of Susman Godfrey For OpenAI: attorney information not yet available

item.title: Target apologizes for children's clown Halloween costume after backlash
item.description: Target apologized on Monday and said it had pulled a Halloween costume from sale depicting a circus clown that critics said evoked Blackface and minstrel shows.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Brown, Neil Kanatt
item.content:encoded:
Target (TGT.N) apologized on Monday and said it had pulled a Halloween costume from sale depicting a circus clown that critics said evoked Blackface and minstrel shows. The product, sold as the "Kids' Glows Under Blacklight Circus Clown Halloween Costume," prompted a backlash on social media, with some consumers saying it resembled a racist caricature.

View this post on Instagram

"As a company, we know we got this wrong, and we are deeply sorry," Target said in a statement. "The costume is offensive and should never have been part of our assortment. It is no longer available for sale." It is the latest optics headache for the U.S. retailer as it tries to right its ship after a stretch of poor sales. The company also faced criticism over its handling of products in its 2023 [USN:L8N37R4OP TEXT:"Pride Collection"], and for changes to its [USN:L3N3OK1Q5 TEXT:"diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives"] in the wake of President Donald Trump's return to the White House. Target declined to comment on who designed the product - which was sold under the retailer's seasonal Hyde and EEK Boutique brand - or the process by which it was green-lit for sale. In its statement, Target said it was "looking closely at how this happened and what needs to change." Some Black shoppers, who felt [USN:L2N3ON0SZ TEXT:"alienated"] after Target's 2025 DEI [USN:L2N3PB0T4 TEXT:"rollbacks"], expressed fresh disappointment on Monday. Sheletta Brundidge, a Minneapolis-area business leader, views the costume as an indirect result of the DEI decision. "You rolled back diversity," she said, "so who's in the room, now, to say 'hey, this is wrong?'" Target acknowledged in its statement the costume was "especially hurtful for our Black guests, team members and partners." Though a Target-owned brand, Hyde and EEK products have been resold on websites of retailers like Walmart (WMT.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) , and the marketplace Etsy (ETSY.N) . Reuters did not see the item in question on those sites. A Walmart spokeswoman said she had no knowledge of that item being sold. Amazon and Etsy did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Target, which has had back-to-back strong quarters, is beginning to see [USN:L4N44F12R TEXT:"results"] from efforts to cut prices and freshen its merchandise, with new CEO Michael Fiddelke so far earning plaudits from Wall Street. But the company - which cannot compete with Walmart and Costco on price - has little room for error when it comes to managerial or optical missteps, said Brett Husslein, an analyst at Morningstar. "As Target begins to gain traction in repairing its brand reputation, this is exactly the kind of stuff they want to avoid," he said, adding that any headwind - optical, managerial, or macroeconomic - "could lead to further market share losses." Target's shares were up 2.7% in afternoon trading.

item.title: Trump's approval holds at record low as US support for Iran war falls, Reuters Ipsos poll finds
item.description: U.S. public approval of the war with Iran fell to its lowest level since the conflict's early days, helping to hold President Donald Trump's popularity at a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: U.S. public approval of the war with Iran fell to its lowest level since the conflict's early days, helping to hold President Donald Trump's popularity at a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. The four-day poll showed just 31% of Americans support U.S. military action against Iran, down from 37% in a March Reuters/Ipsos poll and 34% earlier this month. The decline was driven by fewer self-identified Republicans backing the conflict. Some 69% of Republican respondents support the war, compared with 77% in March. The war has been dragging on Trump's public standing this year, and for the second survey in a row just 33% of respondents said they approved of the Republican's performance in the White House, the lowest level in Reuters/Ipsos polls in Trump's first or second term. Trump has told Americans that the war - which started with U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28 - is necessary to keep Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. The conflict has cooled in recent months but Iran has kept in place a de facto blockade of oil exports from the region, which has pushed U.S. gasoline prices near record highs. Trump has vowed to ramp up economic pressure on Iran and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced a possible expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with the country, but stopped short of actually imposing penalties, a sign of how thorny the conflict has become for the administration. FEARS OF A LONG WAR Some 83% of the country thinks the war will go on "for an extended period of time," the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll found, up from 80% earlier this month. Trump campaigned ahead of the 2024 presidential election on promises to control inflation and avoid lengthy military conflicts. Six months into the war with Iran, U.S. gasoline prices are more than a dollar higher per gallon than they were before the war. That is weighing on Trump's Republican allies who will be defending narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections. Independent voters in the poll favored Democrats over Republicans - 33% to 19% - when asked who they would vote for in congressional elections if the election were held today. The poll surveyed 1,215 U.S. adults nationwide and had a margin of error of 3 percentage points in either direction.

item.title: Federer playing Flushing Meadows exhibition in long overdue US Open sendoff
item.description: Roger Federer will make a long-awaited curtain call for his adoring fans at Flushing Meadows on Tuesday as the man who defined a generation of tennis plays in an exhibition event ahead of the U.S. Open singles main draw.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Roger Federer will make a long-awaited curtain call for his adoring fans at Flushing Meadows on Tuesday as the man who defined a generation of tennis plays in an exhibition event ahead of the U.S. Open singles main draw. His final U.S. Open match in 2019 lacked the romantic sendoff that fans have come to expect for former champions, as the Swiss exited in the quarter-finals with many expecting him to return to play at the event again. But he was absent from the U.S Open in 2020 and played in his final slam at Wimbledon in 2021, leaving the New York tournament he once dominated without a proper farewell. "It really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you, goodbye, which is I think important for some," said Federer, whose five consecutive wins are unmatched by any man in the Open Era. "For me it is, and it's a nice thing to do." Tuesday's exhibition, "US Open: Roger Federer - An Icon Returns to NY," was fetching upwards of $2,000 on Ticketmaster's resale platform on Monday, and the Swiss Maestro said he only hoped he could hit the right notes after a long layoff. "It's nerve-wracking, to be honest. I haven't played a single set in - I don't know - maybe five years. Don't know how it's going to go tomorrow," he told reporters. "There's a lot of uncertainty, but a lot of happiness that I can return." Federer will play alongside fellow retired greats Andy Roddick, Andre Agassi and John McEnroe at Arthur Ashe Stadium, where newly un-retired American Serena Williams is due to play mixed doubles with Carlos Alcaraz earlier in the day. The 44-year-old Williams' return to New York had Flushing Meadows buzzing on Monday, as fans had already begun to flood the plaza to catch some of the singles qualifying tournament. Asked if he would ever consider accepting a wild card to the singles competition, Federer, who is only one year Williams' senior, was emphatic: "No, no, no, no, no, no." "I've got just way too many obstacles and I'm too busy - I'm barely finding time to play any exos," said Federer, who is due to be inducted in the Tennis Hall of Fame on Saturday. "The body is done." The U.S. Open men's and women's singles main draw begins on Sunday.

item.title: Law firm Paul Weiss taps new Supreme Court practice head after Shanmugam exit
item.description: Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year. Jay, who has argued 19 cases before the U.S. Supreme Court, joins Paul Weiss as a Washington, D.C.-based partner, the firm said on Monday. He has represented clients including Teva Pharmaceuticals, Varsity Brands and B&B Hardware. Shanmugam, who previously led the Supreme Court practice at Paul Weiss, [USN:L6N4161HM TEXT:"departed"] with Masha Hansford in April to launch a new practice at law firm Davis Polk. Jay practiced at Goodwin for 14 years. He previously worked as an assistant to the Solicitor General. Earlier in his career he was a clerk to former U.S. Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia. Jay told Reuters that he was eager to join Paul Weiss as the New York firm grows its litigation department. Paul Weiss has hired a handful of litigation partners this year, including former U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission deputy enforcement director Antonia Apps in February. The firm has also seen litigator departures, including a pair of partners who joined Linklaters in July.

item.title: Hyundai Motor's union reaches tentative wage deal, averting more strikes
item.description: Hyundai Motor's South Korean union said on Tuesday it has reached a tentative agreement with management, averting further production losses after staging its first full strike in a decade on Friday, following a series of partial stoppages.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hyundai Motor's (005380.KS) South Korean union said on Tuesday it has reached a tentative agreement with management, averting further production losses after staging its first full strike in a decade on Friday, following a series of partial stoppages. The union had demanded higher bonuses, an increase in the retirement age, and job protections against artificial intelligence and automation. The tentative agreement includes a base salary increase of 100,000 won ($72.31) per month plus a performance bonus equivalent to 400% of base pay and additional payouts in cash and bonuses. The retirement age will be extended from the current 60 upon amendment of a relevant law, without reducing salary for the first few years after 60, the union said. From next year until 2028, 500 new technical workers will be hired. Hyundai Motor did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The union had demanded the company set aside 30% of net income for bonuses and guarantee job security, raising concerns over the growing adoption of robotics and artificial intelligence on assembly lines. Regarding union demands on job security related to AI, the two sides agreed to discuss matters related to employment when it comes to rolling out new businesses, according to the agreement seen by Reuters. Hyundai, which owns humanoid robot maker Boston Dynamics, has said it plans to deploy humanoid robots at its U.S. plant in Georgia from 2028, with the aim of expanding their use across its production sites. ($1 = 1,382.8900 won)

item.title: Haiti gang raid leaves 30 dead, as residents demand stronger protections
item.description: At least 30 people were killed in an overnight gang raid on a neighborhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the town's Mayor Jean Massillon said on Monday, prompting anger over lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks.
item.dc:creator: Harold Isaac, Ives Surin
item.content:encoded: At least 30 people were killed in an overnight gang raid on a neighborhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the town's Mayor Jean Massillon said on Monday, prompting anger over lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks. The hillside community of Kenscoff, in a strategic position overlooking routes into the capital, has suffered a dozen attacks by armed gangs since last year, forcing thousands to flee their homes. Powerful gangs under a broad alliance have for years cemented their influence over Haiti's capital and expanded to nearby regions, despite attempts by foreign nations to reinforce the country's outgunned police. Haitian rights group RNDDH estimated 30 to 40 people were killed and 15 to 20 wounded in the raid, which began around 10:30 p.m. local time, but said it was difficult to assess a complete tally. Even as Haiti's government decried a "heinous attack" and promised to reinforce security, residents demanded the local police chief step down, saying officers failed to protect people killed just minutes from the police station. Haiti's national police did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "Kenscoff will not be abandoned," the prime minister's office said on social media. "The government's authority will be restored, without weakness and without delay." FORCED TO FLEE KENSCOFF Attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 saw more than 260 people killed and 200 homes destroyed or set on fire, forcing 3,000 people to flee, according to U.N. estimates. Nearly a dozen more attacks have taken place since, including rapes, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft. "My family are victims," said Coriolan Kendy, standing by his cousin's body, lying on the road in a blood-stained sheet. "People in Kenscoff are suffering and the government is to blame." Another resident, Orisme, who did not share his last name, pleaded for the prime minister's support. "We live in humiliation and they do nothing for us," he said. Some residents said several dozen police had tried to rebuff the armed men during the night, and some were injured. They added that they did not identify gang members among the dead. Local media said several houses were set on fire, including the home of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert. Kenscoff overlooks routes into Petion-Ville — home to several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government — as well as a major road from the capital into southern Haiti. The violence may deepen concerns over Haiti's ability to [USN:S0N41D00K TEXT:"hold an election"] in December, its first in a decade. Successive governments have repeatedly postponed elections as armed gangs have expanded their influence. The U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force, which is mandated to help police fight gangs, aims to reach a capacity of more than 5,500 troops this autumn. A spokesperson did not immediately respond to questions on whether the troops were reinforcing Kenscoff security.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE Japan eyes tax breaks for non-core business sales in governance reform push, sources say
item.description: Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Makiko Yamazaki, Miho Uranaka
item.content:encoded: Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said. The plan would remove a major obstacle to companies shedding non-core businesses and redeploying capital into growth areas, in what could become one of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's most significant initiatives to advance corporate governance reform. Under the plan, roughly 30% corporate tax on gains from sales of non-core businesses would be deferred indefinitely, provided companies reinvest the proceeds within several years in acquisitions aligned with their core operations and commit to investing in those businesses, one of the sources said. The proposal is expected to be submitted as part of tax reform requests due at the end of this month, with details to be worked out before a final tax reform package for the next fiscal year is approved at year-end, said one of the sources, who declined to be identified as the matter is still private. POOR CAPITAL ALLOCATION The initiative is modelled on Germany's tax reform in the early 2000s, which largely exempted corporations from taxes on gains from share disposals, helping dismantle the country's dense network of cross-shareholdings and making it easier for companies to reshape their business portfolios. Non-core businesses often remain trapped within sprawling Japanese conglomerates because gains from divestitures are taxed, reducing the incentive to transfer assets to owners better positioned to extract value from them. The result is often inefficient capital allocation. A recent government study found that about 65% of Japanese companies' invested capital remains tied up in businesses that fail to earn their cost of capital, largely offsetting value created by higher-performing units. Such capital trapped in low-return operations is seen as limiting growth investment and weighing on long-term corporate value. Japan has already introduced a range of measures to promote business overhauls over the years, including spin-off tax rules in 2017 and a partial spin-off regime in 2023, but business divestitures taking advantage of those rules have remained relatively limited. A 2020 industry ministry report showed Japanese companies often lack clear divestment criteria and have traditionally prioritised maintaining group size, employment and corporate stability over portfolio reshaping. The tax reform, if implemented, is likely to boost already sizzling M&A activity in Japan. Deal activity involving Japanese companies last year more than doubled from the previous year to a record $353 billion, according to LSEG. Divestitures of Japanese businesses accounted for $44.7 billion of that total.

item.title: Monedas caen en medio de cautela de mercados a la espera de datos y Fed
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina iniciaron la semana con bajas, en medio de la cautela que ronda los mercados en una semana en la que se esperan datos y presentaciones de banqueros centrales que puedan dar orientación sobre el futuro de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina iniciaron la semana con bajas, en medio de la cautela que ronda los mercados en una semana en la que se esperan datos y presentaciones de banqueros centrales que puedan dar orientación sobre el futuro de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos. * La mirada, además, seguía puesta en la evolución de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro, cuya alza de las últimas semanas ha generado preocupaciones sobre los costos del endeudamiento. * La cautela en las monedas era también generada por los acontecimientos sobre Oriente Medio, luego de que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunció una ampliación de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que mantengan vínculos comerciales con Irán en todo el mundo. * El dólar avanzó a nivel global tras la ampliación de las sanciones contra Irán y la imposición de aranceles adicionales a los productos procedentes de Canadá. * La semana también estará marcada por los comentarios del presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, en el simposio de Jackson Hole, sobre la orientación de las tasas de interés. * El peso mayorista argentino se depreció un 0,66% al nivel mínimo histórico en 1.510 por cada dólar, su nivel mínimo histórico. El banco central (BCRA) argentino acumuló compras por 11 millones de dólares con el inicio de esta semana. * "El dólar mayorista quebró la barrera de los 1.500 (pesos) porque contenerlo a medida que pasa el tiempo exige esfuerzos mayores en términos de comprar menos reservas y subir tasas", dijo a Reuters Roberto Gerreto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. * "Así, subas graduales del dólar van a permitir que no se atrase, facilitando la acumulación de reservas y no agregando estrés en las tasas. La clave será que no tenga ningún componente anunciado o sistemático, porque ello daría incentivos a dolarizar como ocurre cuando hay un 'crawling peg' formal", agregó. * Mientras, el índice S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires trepó un 2,81%, apoyada por el avance de acciones del rubro financiero. El Merval cayó un 1,2% la semana previa. * El peso mexicano bajaba hacia el cierre un 0,33%, a 16,9516 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, subió un ligero 0,06%, a 65.770,85 * "La moneda local enfrenta presiones por el fortalecimiento del dólar, el menor apetito por activos de mayor riesgo y las tensiones comerciales en Norteamérica, ante la cuarta revisión bilateral entre México y Estados Unidos, prevista para septiembre", dijo la correduría Monex. * La inflación general de México avanzó en la primera quincena de agosto, aunque menos de lo previsto, mientras que el índice subyacente se desaceleró de forma inesperada. * El real brasileño cedió un 0,23% a 5,1534 unidades por dólar, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) ganó un 0,6% a 172.055 puntos. * El peso colombiano terminó con baja de un 0,67% a 3.057 unidades por dólar, alejándose de máximos de casi ocho años; mientras que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) se valorizó un 2,09% a 2.510,68 puntos. * El peso chileno , subió un 0,25%, en 912,50/912,80 unidades por dólar. En tanto, El índice principal de la Bolsa de Comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , escaló un 1,76%, a 11.537,97 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó la jornada con una leve depreciación del 0,06% a 3,3460/3,3470 unidades por dólar. En tanto que, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) revirtió leves alzas y perdió un 0,18% a 1573,49 puntos.

item.title: Rendimiento de bonos EEUU cae mientras el Tesoro evalúa un cambio en su política de recompra
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos de Estados Unidos caía el lunes, tras conocerse que el Departamento del Tesoro podría recurrir a su cuenta en efectivo para financiar un aumento de las recompras de deuda, mientras que los precios del petróleo retrocedieron.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos de Estados Unidos caía el lunes, tras conocerse que el Departamento del Tesoro podría recurrir a su cuenta en efectivo para financiar un aumento de las recompras de deuda, mientras que los precios del petróleo retrocedieron. * La CNBC dio a conocer la noticia menos de una semana después de que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunciara que el Gobierno duplicará, como mínimo, sus recompras de deuda a largo plazo, una medida inesperada que avivó la especulación sobre un enfoque más intervencionista para frenar el aumento de los rendimientos. * Esta medida supondría un cambio de rumbo, ya que las recompras están pensadas para ser neutras en términos de efectivo y se han financiado mediante emisiones, según explicó Molly Brooks, de TD Securities. * Los operadores siguen sopesando las implicaciones, sobre todo porque la decisión se produjo al margen del calendario habitual de refinanciación del Tesoro. A algunos les preocupa que la medida sea contraproducente y socave la confianza en el enfoque "regular y predecible" de la agencia respecto a la emisión de deuda. * "Si seguimos viendo este tipo de titulares que indican que podrían estar acelerando un poco las cosas, esa naturaleza regular y predecible podría, de hecho, aumentar la prima de plazo de los bonos del Tesoro a largo plazo", señaló Brooks. * Bessent afirmó el lunes que Estados Unidos continuaría con su programa habitual de subastas de bonos del Tesoro. * Esta situación complica aún más las perspectivas sobre las tasas de interés, ya que varias autoridades monetarias de la Reserva Federal han abogado por alzas en medio de una inflación persistentemente elevada. * Los operadores de futuros sobre los fondos federales están valorando en un 44% la probabilidad de un alza de tasas en la reunión de política monetaria del banco central de septiembre, cifra que se eleva al 78% para diciembre. * El rendimiento de los bonos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en línea con las expectativas de tasas, cotizaba estable en el 4,234%, y el de las notas referenciales a 10 años perdía 3,99 puntos básicos, al 4,698%. * La curva de rendimiento entre la deuda a dos y 10 años se aplanaba a 46 puntos básicos.

item.title: Peso argentino toca nivel mínimo histórico
item.description: El peso argentino en el mercado interbancario anotó el lunes su nivel mínimo histórico, con aval del Gobierno, tras romper la barrera psicológica de las 1.500 unidades por dólar para la venta.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso argentino en el mercado interbancario anotó el lunes su nivel mínimo histórico, con aval del Gobierno, tras romper la barrera psicológica de las 1.500 unidades por dólar para la venta. Los analistas coinciden en que es saludable la tendencia ya que hay un consenso generalizado de cierto atraso cambiario, en un país donde el dólar se usa como ahorro ante el resguardo inflacionario. Por su parte, las plazas de acciones y bonos del país sudamericano registraron mejoras dispares luego de finalizar en baja la semana previa ante la clara postura de prudencia por parte de los inversores. En el segmento mayorista , el peso nacional se depreció un 0,66% al nivel mínimo histórico en 1.510 por cada dólar, luego de cerrar la semana anterior en 1.500 unidades. "El dólar mayorista quebró la barrera de los 1.500 (pesos) porque contenerlo a medida que pasa el tiempo exige esfuerzos mayores en términos de comprar menos reservas y subir tasas", dijo a Reuters Roberto Geretto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. "Así, subas graduales del dólar van a permitir que no se atrase, facilitando la acumulación de reservas y no agregando estrés en las tasas. La clave será que no tenga ningún componente anunciado o sistemático, porque ello daría incentivos a dolarizar como ocurre cuando hay un 'crawling peg' formal", agregó. El banco central (BCRA) argentino acumuló compras por 11 millones de dólares con el inicio de esta semana. Hasta la semana anterior, en "agosto las compras (del BCRA) acumulan 466 millones de dólares, un promedio de 33 millones de dólares diarios que profundiza la desaceleración frente a julio (103 millones diarios) y queda por debajo de junio (68 millones de dólares) y mayo (137 millones de dólares)", explicó el agente de compensación y liquidación Cohen. El índice S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires mejoró un firme 2,81% al cierre, apoyado por el avance de acciones del rubro financiero, contra una caída del 1,2% la semana previa. "Pese al freno del deterioro reciente, el mercado mantiene la cautela ante la duda de si este movimiento constituye una mejora de fondo o un mero rebote técnico", expresó la consultora Wise Capital. En tanto, los bonos soberanos en el segmento extrabursátil mejoraron apenas un 0,1% promedio, tras finalizar con un retroceso de 1,8% la semana pasada. El riesgo país, elaborado por el banco JP. Morgan, retrocedía algunos escalones hasta los 503 puntos básicos (2000 GMT). El llamado Índice de Confianza en el Gobierno (ICG) de la Universidad Torcuato Di Tella subió 2,4 puntos porcentuales a 41,2% en agosto, marcando la mayor mejora mensual desde noviembre. "La confianza en el Gobierno (del libertario Javier Milei) se mantiene elevada en relación a otras presidencias de este siglo", dijo el agente de liquidación y compensación Facimex. "La confianza en el Gobierno es clave por su correlación con los resultados electorales para el oficialismo", acotó.

item.title: S&P 500 y Nasdaq caen presionados por acciones tecnológicas; inversores analizan medidas sobre Irán
item.description: Los índices S&P 500 y Nasdaq descendieron el lunes, lastrados por las acciones tecnológicas, mientras los inversores sopesaban la nueva presión económica estadounidense contra Irán, a la espera esta semana de los resultados del gigante de la IA Nvidia y de un informe clave sobre la inflación.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Azhar, Purvi Agarwal, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Los índices S&P 500 y Nasdaq descendieron el lunes, lastrados por las acciones tecnológicas, mientras los inversores sopesaban la nueva presión económica estadounidense contra Irán, a la espera esta semana de los resultados del gigante de la IA Nvidia y de un informe clave sobre la inflación. * El Gobierno de Donald Trump anunció el lunes una posible ampliación de las sanciones a los países que mantienen relaciones comerciales con Irán, en lo que denominó un "Día D económico", pero no llegó a imponer sanciones. * Las acciones de semiconductores cayeron, arrastrando al índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia (.SOX) . Nvidia (NVDA.O) bajó, al igual que Micron Technology (MU.O) y Broadcom (AVGO.O) , presionando al índice de tecnología de la información del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) . * El sentimiento hacia las empresas tecnológicas también se vio afectado por la creciente oposición política a los centros de datos de IA. * El gobernador de Texas, Greg Abbott, lanzó una de las advertencias más contundentes hasta la fecha por parte de un republicano a la industria de la IA, afirmando que las firmas de centros de datos "cavaron su propia tumba" y merecen el rechazo que enfrentan tras no lograr el apoyo de la comunidad, informó Axios el domingo. * Sin embargo, el índice financiero (.SPSY) subió, con JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) y Visa (V.N) al alza. También contribuyeron a mantener a flote al índice Dow Jones. * Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 21,37 puntos, o un 0,28%, a 7.653,00 unidades. El Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) bajó 200,80 puntos, o un 0,77%, a 25.979,66 unidades; y el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) subió 141,67 puntos, o un 0,27%, a 53.418,68 unidades. * Se espera que los resultados trimestrales del gigante de la IA, Nvidia, sean otro catalizador clave para los mercados. Cualquier señal de desaceleración del crecimiento podría reavivar la preocupación por las elevadas valoraciones. * Los mercados también estarán atentos al informe de Gastos de Consumo Personal, el indicador de inflación preferido de la Fed, que se publicará el miércoles.

item.title: As US border reopens to Mexican cattle, concerns persist over screwworm spread
item.description: Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening.
item.dc:creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening. The reopening marks the first easing of a U.S. ban imposed more than a year ago to keep out the flesh-eating pest, as imports [USN:FWN43Q0OT TEXT:"resumed"] initially through Arizona . The plan has drawn criticism from some U.S. cattle groups and state officials who argue that resuming imports could increase screwworm risks even as the parasite continues to spread in northern Mexico and has already been detected in Texas and New Mexico. Mexican Agriculture Minister Columba Lopez said authorities would reinforce the dispersal of sterile flies in Sonora and Chihuahua, a key eradication strategy aimed at preventing the parasite from reproducing. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins told reporters on Monday that the USDA feels it has "taken every step to protect the American (cattle) herd and the American consumer, and so now we can slowly begin to reopen the ports." The USDA plans to open two more New Mexico ports, one in 30 days and another in 60 days, Rollins said. "We don't plan to open any Texas ports anytime soon just because that is where the real activity is," Rollins said. The USDA has identified 46 cases of screwworm in New Mexico and Texas, with two currently active, according to the agency's website. NEW CASES IN MEXICO A USDA website on Monday said it reopened the Douglas, Arizona, port to cattle imports from Mexico "guided by overlapping safeguards and a science-based import protocol" agreed upon by the two countries. The USDA will next evaluate the reopening of ports in Santa Teresa and Columbus, New Mexico, to cattle, bison, and horses. "The opening of ports may be paused if USDA identifies increased risk in Sonora or Chihuahua via post-opening audits or other observations/information," the site said. The reopening will begin with exports of 700 head of cattle per day during the first week, increasing to 900 per day in the second week and gradually rising to around 1,300 per day, according to Mexico’s National Confederation of Livestock Organizations (CNOG). If additional Chihuahua border crossings are reopened in the fourth quarter, Mexico could export up to 200,000 head of cattle in 2026, with an estimated value of about $420 million at U.S. market prices, CNOG said. Its base scenario for 2027 projects exports of 1.09 million head of cattle, valued at roughly $2.1 billion in the U.S. market. Chihuahua, one of Mexico's most important cattle-exporting states, has reported 183 confirmed screwworm cases since detecting its first case in July, while neighboring Sonora state has reported two confirmed cases after announcing its first detection last week. Sonora has activated emergency surveillance and containment protocols, while Chihuahua has intensified inspections, livestock movement controls and treatment campaigns to prevent further spread. The sterile insect technique works by releasing millions of sterilized screwworm flies that mate with wild females but produce no offspring, gradually driving down the pest population. Mexico recently opened a sterile-fly production plant in Chiapas, while the U.S. is building its own production facility in Texas, expected to be completed by the [USN:L6N4470WS TEXT:"spring of 2027"]. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum referred to the sterile-fly technique as a "modern" and "effective" way to fight screwworm. "That allows us to open the border," Sheinbaum said in her daily press conference.

item.title: A medida que la frontera de EEUU vuelve a abrirse al ganado mexicano, persiste preocupación por propagación del gusano barrenador
item.description: México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos. La reapertura supone la primera flexibilización de la prohibición impuesta por Estados Unidos hace más de un año para impedir la entrada de esta plaga carnívora, ya que las importaciones se reanudaron inicialmente a través de Arizona. El plan ha suscitado críticas por parte de algunas asociaciones ganaderas estadounidenses y de autoridades estatales, que argumentan que la reanudación de las importaciones podría aumentar el riesgo de infestación por el gusano barrenador, en un momento en que el parásito sigue propagándose por el norte de México y ya se ha detectado en Texas y Nuevo México. La secretaria de Agricultura de México, Columba López, afirmó que las autoridades reforzarían la liberación de moscas estériles en Sonora y Chihuahua, una estrategia clave de erradicación destinada a impedir que el parásito se reproduzca. "Vamos a mantener nosotros todo el sistema de trazabilidad desde la nacencia hasta que coloquemos el ganado del otro lado", dijo López en un enlace desde Sonora a la conferencia de prensa matutina de la presidente Claudia Sheinbaum. "Y la otra parte es reforzar la dispersión de moscas (vamos a) mantener muchísimos controles de seguridad", añadió. La secretaria de Agricultura de Estados Unidos, Brooke Rollins, dijo el lunes a periodistas que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos (USDA por su sigla en inglés) considera que ha "tomado todas las medidas necesarias para proteger el ganado estadounidense y al consumidor estadounidense, por lo que ahora podemos empezar poco a poco a reabrir los puertos". El USDA tiene previsto abrir dos puertos más en Nuevo México, uno dentro de 30 días y otro dentro de 60 días, indicó Rollins. "No tenemos previsto abrir ningún puerto de Texas a corto plazo, simplemente porque es allí donde se concentra la actividad real", afirmó. NUEVOS CASOS EN MÉXICO El lunes, la página en internet del USDA informó de que se había reabierto el puerto de Douglas, en Arizona, a las importaciones de ganado procedente de México, "guiándose por medidas de seguridad complementarias y un protocolo de importación con base científica" acordado por ambos países. El USDA evaluará la reapertura de los puertos de Santa Teresa y Columbus, en Nuevo México, al ganado vacuno, los bisontes y los caballos. "La apertura de los puertos podría suspenderse si el USDA detecta un aumento del riesgo en Sonora o Chihuahua a través de auditorías posteriores a la apertura u otras observaciones o información", indicó en el sitio. La reapertura comenzará con exportaciones de 700 cabezas de ganado al día durante la primera semana, pasando a 900 al día en la segunda semana y aumentando gradualmente hasta alcanzar unas 1,300 al día, dijo la Confederación Nacional de Organizaciones Ganaderas (CNOG) de México en un comunicado. Si se reabren más pasos fronterizos de Chihuahua en el cuarto trimestre, México podría exportar hasta 200,000 cabezas de ganado en 2026, con un valor estimado de unos 420 millones de dólares a precios del mercado estadounidense, según la CNOG. Su escenario base para 2027 prevé exportaciones de 1.09 millones de cabezas de ganado, valoradas en aproximadamente 2,100 millones de dólares en el mercado estadounidense. Chihuahua, uno de los estados mexicanos más importantes en la exportación de ganado, ha notificado 183 casos confirmados de gusano barrenador desde que detectó su primer caso en julio, mientras que el vecino estado Sonora ha notificado dos casos confirmados tras anunciar su primera detección la semana pasada. Sonora ha activado protocolos de vigilancia y contención de emergencia, mientras que Chihuahua ha intensificado las inspecciones, los controles de movimiento de ganado y las campañas de tratamiento para evitar una mayor propagación. La técnica de insectos estériles consiste en liberar millones de moscas esterilizadas que se aparean con hembras silvestres pero no producen descendencia, lo que reduce gradualmente la población de la plaga. México ha inaugurado recientemente una planta de producción de moscas estériles en Chiapas, mientras que Estados Unidos está construyendo su propia instalación de producción en Texas, cuya finalización está prevista para la primavera de 2027. La presidenta Sheinbaum se refirió a la técnica de la mosca estéril como una forma "moderna" y "eficaz" de combatir al gusano barrenador. "Eso nos permite que se abra la frontera", afirmó la mandataria en su rueda de prensa.

item.title: Capricor's Duchenne drug gets three-month FDA extension after new data submission
item.description: Capricor Therapeutics said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review period for its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR.O) said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review period for its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months. The delay follows Capricor's submission of new 24-month data from its late-stage study, along with extra analyses, to support a refined proposed indication focused on upper limb function, the trial's main goal. The therapy, deramiocel, last year failed to get FDA's [USN:L4N3T80S4 TEXT:"approval"] to treat cardiomyopathy, or a heart muscle disease, in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The regulator said the treatment did not meet efficacy requirements and asked for more data. Earlier this year, Capricor resubmitted its application with new data, and was expecting a decision by August 22. But last month, an FDA advisory panel [USN:L4N43V2DJ TEXT:"voted against"] the therapy's effectiveness data, while the [USN:L4N43T0YE TEXT:"agency staff flagged concerns"] about changes to how the company measured trial results. Following this, Capricor Chief Executive Linda Marban said the company will submit an amendment with new data focused on improving upper limb muscle function. The health regulator has accepted the amendment, citing the high unmet medical need for Duchenne patients, and classified the submission as a "major amendment" and set the new deadline to November 22, Capricor said. Shares of the company rose 15% to $7.25. Marbán said the additional follow-up data gives the company "one of the most extensive clinical datasets evaluating upper limb function in Duchenne," and that the trial had [USN:L4N3X90YA TEXT:"met its main goal"] with a statistically significant benefit. Deramiocel is being developed to treat Duchenne, a rare genetic disease that affects about 15,000 people in the United States, primarily boys. The key question remains whether the new data and analyses are sufficient to "address the FDA's concerns and support approval for the refined indication focused on upper limb function," said H.C. Wainwright analysts.

item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah
item.description: A private arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah with back pay after she was fired over social media posts about Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A private arbitrator has ordered The Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah with back pay, after the newspaper fired her in September over social media posts about conservative activist [USN:L2N3UX0YE TEXT:"Charlie Kirk's assassination"]. The ruling, made public by the Democracy Defenders Fund on Monday, comes as the Post's opinion section faces scrutiny following a push by owner Jeff Bezos to focus on [USN:L2N3PH0XF TEXT:"personal liberties and free markets"]. Here are some more details: Private arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa found the newspaper "did not have good and sufficient cause" to terminate Attiah and had "violated" its labor agreement. "The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct," she wrote. "This decision confirms what we've said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion journalist, and doing that job is not misconduct," said Attiah. A Washington Post spokesperson said the newspaper respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further. The dispute began after Attiah's posts on social media platform Bluesky following Kirk's September 2025 assassination, including one in which she noted Kirk's past comments on Black women. The Post had said in its termination letter that Attiah's posts violated its social media policy, which requires employees' online activity to be respectful and not undermine the integrity of the newspaper's journalism. In February, The Washington Post [USN:L6N3Z015A TEXT:"began layoffs"] impacting a third of its employees, across its international, editing, metro and sports desks amid mounting financial losses. The New York Times first reported the arbitration decision earlier in the day.

item.title: US threatens countries doing business with Iran, but holds off on penalties for now
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday warned countries to cut their business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions as part of what it billed as an "economic D-Day," but the Treasury Department stopped short of actually imposing penalties.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday warned countries to cut their business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions as part of what it billed as an "economic D-Day," but the Treasury Department stopped short of actually imposing penalties. As the war with Iran nears its six-month mark, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. was launching an "economic onslaught" against Iran's financial connections around the globe. But he declined to say what specific countries would be targeted, or when those penalties would take effect. The Treasury Department announced new sanctions on 60 individuals, entities and vessels but that list did not include any of the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade. "Why would I want to blow up the global financial system? We believe that it is important to level set and give people a cure period, but they should know that that will move very quickly and that we are serious," Bessent told a press conference. China has for several years been the biggest buyer of Iranian oil, and Washington has intensified its efforts to clamp down on Chinese purchases, but has so far stopped short of targeting Chinese banks with sanctions. Asked whether the Treasury was now prepared to move against a Chinese bank, he said that no country was out of the reach of U.S. sanctions, adding: "If they facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted." With Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping scheduled to meet in Washington in late September, new sanctions on Chinese banks could sour prospects for extending a deal struck last November to keep Chinese rare earths flowing and cap U.S. tariffs. Tuesday's action targeted other businesses in China, the UAE, Singapore and several other countries, including a cooking-oil refinery in France. Bessent said the U.S. was expanding the scope of commercial activities that could be subject to secondary sanctions in five sectors of the Iranian economy: digital assets, gold, technology, aviation and shipping. He said he previewed a "major announcement" of sanctions on a financial institution by the end of the week but a Treasury spokesperson did not respond to a request for more information. LONG CAMPAIGN Daniel Fried, a former U.S. State Department sanctions coordinator who is now with the Atlantic Council, said that the announcement "did not live up to the hype," but economic pressure is better than restarting military conflict. The pressure campaign on Iran will take time to work and patience and possibly require some concessions on the part of the Trump administration to secure cooperation, he said. "You're going to have to get the Gulf countries to agree, and you're going to have to listen to what they want, and be steady," Fried said. Trump's war with Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher worldwide, is about to hit its six-month mark. While heavy fighting has subsided, diplomatic efforts to end the war have stalled and oil and raw material shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, keeping energy prices elevated. Trump's approval rating has fallen to a low point, with just 33% of Americans in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll approving of his performance. He says the economic costs are necessary to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon. DECADES OF SANCTIONS The U.S. has maintained sanctions against Iran for decades, most of which have been aimed at curtailing the country's oil revenues, acquisition of weapons components and cutting off funding for business enterprises controlled by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a dominant force in the Iranian economy. The sanctions bar designated entities from the dollar-based financial system, but Iran has been successful in quickly standing up new front companies, other entities and vessel registrations to evade the sanctions. The Treasury Department has also recently sanctioned independent Chinese "teapot" refineries for buying Iranian oil, and expanded sanctions on the "shadow fleet" of tankers transporting Iranian oil. Tehran has managed to weather decades of U.S. sanctions but the naval blockade that the U.S. imposed has inflicted severe economic damage on the country. That already curbed Chinese offers to purchase Iranian crude, [USN:L1N44I07T TEXT:"Reuters reported on Friday"], which may lessen the impact of secondary sanctions on China. Earlier this month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States could maintain the naval blockade indefinitely, which could keep oil prices elevated, potentially stirring U.S. voter anger ahead of congressional elections in November. Treasury Department data shows the U.S. has imposed Iran-related sanctions on more than 1,000 people, vessels and aircraft since Trump began his second term in 2025. Recent measures have targeted Iran's shadow oil fleet, shipping insurers, weapons-procurement network, and digital exchanges, freezing an estimated $500 billion in Iran-linked cryptocurrency. Bessent singled out Iran's Bank Melli, which continues to operate branches in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. "Every branch of Bank Melli must be shuttered and dark," he said.

item.title: Crudo cae más de 2 dólares pese a nuevas sanciones de EEUU contra Irán
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cayeron más de 2 dólares por barril el lunes ya que los inversores recogieron beneficios tras las recientes alzas y no prestaron atención a las nuevas sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Irán.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cayeron más de 2 dólares por barril el lunes ya que los inversores recogieron beneficios tras las recientes alzas y no prestaron atención a las nuevas sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Irán. * Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron con caída de 2,22 dólares, o un 2,35%, hasta los 92,17 dólares, mientras que el crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate cayó 2,05 dólares por barril, un 2,35% menos, hasta situarse en 85,01 dólares. * El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunció el lunes una ampliación de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que mantengan vínculos comerciales con Irán en todo el mundo, en un momento en que Washington intensifica significativamente la presión económica sobre Teherán. * Lo anterior se produjo tras las amenazas de Trump de "guerra económica y aislamiento a una escala sin precedentes" contra Teherán la semana pasada. * "No hay muchas novedades en las declaraciones de Bessent, más allá de lo que ya se había adelantado", afirmó Pavel Molchanov, analista de estrategia de inversión de Raymond James. Añadió que el mercado del petróleo, tras repuntar bastante la semana pasada, registró una toma de beneficios. * Ambos contratos registraron la semana pasada su segunda alza semanal consecutiva, con un aumento superior al 5%. * "La verdadera pregunta ahora es hasta qué punto está dispuesto Washington a aplicar con dureza sanciones secundarias contra los socios comerciales que aún le quedan a Irán", señaló Jorge León, jefe de análisis geopolítico de Rystad Energy. "A menos que China reduzca sustancialmente sus compras, el impacto adicional sobre los ingresos petroleros iraníes podría ser relativamente limitado", añadió. * Irán había condenado los planes de Estados Unidos de anunciar nuevas sanciones y el presidente Masoud Pezeshkian había abogado por una solución diplomática. El jefe del ejército de Pakistán estaba de visita en Teherán el lunes para mantener conversaciones de mediación, antes del anuncio. * Los envíos de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, una ruta por la que antes circulaba una quinta parte del suministro mundial, siguieron viéndose limitados. * Menos de 20 buques de mercancías transitaron por el estrecho de Ormuz el fin de semana, según datos de transporte marítimo publicados el lunes, ya que los bloqueos iraníes y estadounidenses restringen el tráfico a través de este punto estratégico para los envíos de energía.

item.title: Altria, Philip Morris International sign contract manufacturing deals
item.description: Philip Morris International and Altria said on Monday they had entered contract manufacturing arrangements with one another, as Altria looks to grow cigarette imports and exports and take advantage of a tax rebate.
item.dc:creator: Emma Rumney
item.content:encoded: Philip Morris International (PM.N) and Altria (MO.N) said on Monday they had entered contract manufacturing arrangements with one another, as Altria looks to grow cigarette imports and exports and take advantage of a tax rebate. The rebate, known as the "double duty drawback", allows U.S. tobacco companies exporting their products outside the U.S. to claw back federal excise taxes paid on domestically sold products, offering a significant boost to U.S. profits. Altria, which makes Marlboro cigarettes in the United States but does not sell tobacco elsewhere, is [USN:L4N3YU1OO TEXT:"boosting partnerships"] with foreign manufacturers in order to grow its imports and exports. Philip Morris International, which makes Marlboro for the rest of the world and does not sell cigarettes in the United States, said the contract manufacturing deal with Altria does not change this and it has no plans to sell cigarettes in the U.S. Altria said that the arrangement will enhance efficiency and generate "economic benefits". The first shipments are expected in 2027, PMI said. Both companies said they did not expect the arrangements to affect 2026 performance. Altria's shares rose over 2% in early trade. PMI stock was 1.5% higher. Altria said in January it expected a profit boost in the second half of 2026 thanks to similar partnerships with other manufacturers.
